body_html:
To create product variants with structured markup — for instance a phone available in different colors — you’ll need to use the Product-schema and the Product Model-schema.

In this blog-post I’ll mark up an iPhone 6 16GB with 3 different variants: gold, silver and spacegray.

As an added bonus, I’m gonna toggle between the 3 variants without JavaScript, using the wonderful checkbox hack!

A working demo of all this is available here.
Open it in a new tab, and read on …

The basic product-markup, including the data all product-variants have in common: name, description, condition, breadcrumbs and price:

<article itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Product" class="product">
  <section class="product-info">
    <h1 itemprop="name">iPhone 6 - 16GB</h1>
    <p itemprop="description">
      ...
    </p>
    <meta itemprop="itemCondition" content="NewCondition" />
    <div itemprop="offers" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Offer">
      <meta itemprop="category" content="Apple > iPhone > iPhone 6" />
      <span itemprop="price">5799,00</span>
      <span itemprop="priceCurrency">DKK</span>
    </div>
    <span itemprop="image" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/ImageObject">
      <meta itemprop="contentUrl" content="iphone6-gold-select-2014.png" />
    </span>
  </section>
  ...

And now for the variants. Each variant is wrapped in a figure-tag, that will hold the product variant-image as well as a caption and some hidden data:

<figure itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/ProductModel" itemid="#gold">
  <img src="iphone6-gold-select-2014.png" class="product-image" />
  <figcaption>
    <span itemprop="offers" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Offer" class="product-offer">
      <meta itemprop="availability" content="InStock" />
      <button class="product-buy-button">Buy this phone now</button>
    </span>
    <link itemprop="additionalType" href="/" />
    <meta itemprop="name" content="iPhone 6 - 16GB - Gold" />
    <meta itemprop="gtin13" content="12345678901" />
  </figcaption>
</figure>

Each variant has an itemid, which we’ll use later to target the variant directly — as well as a unique gtin-number, a variant-name and an Offer.
All these attributes can be unique per variant.

Here’s a variant that’s currently sold out:

<figure itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/ProductModel" itemid="#silver">
  <img src="iphone6-silver-select-2014.png" class="product-image" />
  <figcaption>
    <span itemprop="offers" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Offer" class="product-offer">
      <meta itemprop="availability" content="OutOfStock" />
      <span class="product-sold-out">Out of Stock. Will be back in stock on April 5th.</span>
    </span>
    <link itemprop="additionalType" href="/" />
    <meta itemprop="name" content="iPhone 6 - 16GB - Silver" />
    <meta itemprop="gtin13" content="12345678902" />
  </figcaption>
</figure>

And now for the promised checkbox-hack! Add this before the product variants-wrapper:

<aside class="product-variant">
  <h2>Choose a finish:</h2>
  <input type="radio" name="img-select-grp" id="gold" value="12345678901" checked /><label for="gold" class="gold">Gold</label>
  <input type="radio" name="img-select-grp" id="silver" value="12345678902" /><label for="silver" class="silver">Silver</label>
  <input type="radio" name="img-select-grp" id="spacegray" value="12345678903" /><label for="spacegray" class="gray">Gray</label>
  ...

The radiobutton will select the given variant, and using :checked in the CSS, we’ll show and hide the various variants.

Go see the demo, and try to paste it’s source to Google’s Structured Data Testing Tool.

Go directly to a variant

To directly link to a specific variant, based on the schemas itemid and the id of the selected variant/radiobutton, use a small piece of JavaScript (modify it and embed it in the load-event of your page):

<script>
  var oSel = document.getElementById(location.hash.slice(1)); 
  if (oSel) oSel.checked = true;
</script>
